fileStructure:
.operator/DECISIONS.md — records the filename-vs-body ownership decision and the rejected option (req 1). The decision is filename ownership stays and body ownership is rejected, so req 2's conditional work does not run.
tests/test-scripts.sh — gains four red-first cases: owned (blocks), unowned (blocks), foreign (reports but does not block), and a check that the statusline and the Stop gate agree on all three (req 3 plus the north star's "no reader disagrees").
tests/floors.env — FLOOR_SHELL raised by the measured passed+skipped count the new cases add (req 5).
.claude-plugin/plugin.json — version 0.13.0 (req 4).
CHANGELOG.md — new top heading `## [0.13.0]` in the same commit as the version bump (req 4; the release gate enforces this).
scripts/lib/partition.sh, scripts/ops-stop-hook.sh, scripts/statusline.sh, scripts/ops-task.sh, scripts/ops-adopt.sh, scripts/ops-verdict.sh, scripts/ops-sessionstart-hook.sh — NOT modified. They are mutated only inside a throwaway worktree to prove each new case can fail.

tasks.title: Record the decision in DECISIONS.md: ownership stays in the filename, body field rejected
tasks.testCycle: `grep -c 'sentinel-ownership-filename' .operator/DECISIONS.md` prints 1. `grep -n 'owner=<sid>' .operator/DECISIONS.md` finds the rejected-option line. `python3 scripts/validate_plugin.py` exits 0 with the same result as before the edit (record the baseline first).
tasks.specExcerpt:
1. Decide filename-vs-body ownership. The decision must weigh: the six hand-copied readers, the builtin-only constraint, the O_EXCL open in ops-task.sh, the legacy migration in ops-sessionstart-hook.sh, and that an unowned sentinel must keep failing CLOSED. Record the decision and the rejected option in DECISIONS.md.
2. If body ownership wins: change ops-task.sh, ops-adopt.sh and ops-verdict.sh to write the field, and the three readers' sentinel_owner_of_name() to read it, keeping the bounded read and the `-L` before `-f` type test.

Goal: Today a pending sentinel's owner is encoded in its filename (`pending/<sid>__<task>`). Six readers hand-copy the parser that splits on the first `__`; two of them (ops-stop-hook.sh, statusline.sh) must stay bash-builtin-only.
steps: Baseline: run `python3 scripts/validate_plugin.py; echo rc=$?` and `bash tests/test-scripts.sh 2>&1 | tail -3`. Write down rc and the passed/failed/skipped counts. If `scripts/validate_plugin.py` is not at that path, run `ls scripts/*.py` and use the real name. This plan did not check the path.

Run `sed -n '1,60p' templates/DECISIONS-header.md` to read the row format and kind enum. Choose a RECORD kind (listed in validate_plugin.DECISIONS_RECORD_KINDS: `grep -n DECISIONS_RECORD_KINDS scripts/validate_plugin.py`). Never use a GATED kind: that arms the deviation gate and blocks Stop.

Before writing, run `grep -n '__' scripts/ops-task.sh | head -40` and confirm three facts. (a) The sentinel is created by one O_EXCL open of `pending/<sid>__<task>`. (b) `ops-adopt.sh` re-owns a sentinel with an atomic `mv`. (c) `scripts/lib/partition.sh` `sentinel_owner_of_name` parses only the NAME and never opens the file.

Append one entry to `.operator/DECISIONS.md` in the header's exact column format. Use id/tag `sentinel-ownership-filename` and kind = the RECORD kind you chose. The decision text is: 'Ownership stays in the filename (`pending/<sid>__<task>`). REJECTED: body field `owner=<sid>`.' Give these reasons: (1) O_EXCL creates the owned name atomically, but a body field means create-then-write, and for that window the sentinel reads as unowned, which fails closed and blocks EVERY session; (2) adopt is an atomic rename today, but a body field would make it read-modify-write under a lock; (3) the builtin-only readers (ops-stop-hook.sh, statusline.sh) would have to open every pending file with a bounded read, and statusline has a ~300ms budget (CR5); (4) the six hand-copied name parsers would become six hand-copied bounded body parsers, so the number of copies does not go down; (5) ops-sessionstart-hook.sh would need a second migration (filename to body) on top of the legacy one; (6) unowned fails closed under either scheme, so that requirement does not favour either option. Consequence: req 2 does not apply; readers and writers are unchanged.

Run the testCycle greps and the validator. Expect rc to equal the baseline. Commit on the current feature branch: `git add .operator/DECISIONS.md && git commit -m 'Sentinel ownership: record filename-vs-body decision (body rejected)'`. If .operator/ is gitignored for DECISIONS.md, say so in the commit report instead of force-adding.

tasks.title: Red-first shell case: my own owned sentinel blocks my Stop
files: tests/test-scripts.sh (append a new `echo "-- Case sentinel owned by this session blocks its Stop"` block after the existing 'sentinel ownership' block; find it with `grep -n 'sentinel ownership' tests/test-scripts.sh`)
produces: Case: sentinel owned by this session blocks its Stop
tasks.testCycle: `bash tests/test-scripts.sh 2>&1 | tail -3` shows passed count = baseline + the new checks, and 0 new failures. In the mutated worktree the same run shows the new case FAILING.
tasks.specExcerpt:
3. Add red-first cases to tests/test-scripts.sh for: owned, unowned (blocks), foreign (reports).

North star: the Stop gate still blocks on mine + unowned. Missed if: any reader and writer disagree on an owner, or an unowned sentinel stops blocking.
steps: Read the existing 'sentinel ownership' case block to learn the fixture helpers: how it builds a temp project with `.operator/pending/`, how it pipes the Stop-hook JSON payload (`session_id`, `cwd`, `stop_hook_active:false`) into `scripts/ops-stop-hook.sh`, and how `check` records a result. Reuse those helpers. Do not write new ones.

Write the case. Create the sentinel with the real WRITER, not a hand-made file: `bash scripts/ops-task.sh own1 --owner SID_A` run inside the fixture. Assert `pending/SID_A__own1` exists as a regular file. Pipe a payload with session_id SID_A into ops-stop-hook.sh and `check` that the exit code is 2. The fixture must not be a git repo so the auto-arm (#85) arms nothing. Give it a fresh `.operator/.stopguard/`, because a leftover marker makes the loop guard stand down.

Prove the case goes red. Run `git worktree add /tmp/own-mut HEAD` and copy the new tests/test-scripts.sh into it. In /tmp/own-mut/scripts/lib/partition.sh, change the mine comparison in `scan_pending` so that an owner equal to the session id goes into the foreign bucket. Run `(cd /tmp/own-mut && bash tests/test-scripts.sh 2>&1 | grep -n 'owned by this session')` and expect FAIL. Keep the mutation in the worktree only: other agents' runs corrupt a shared tree.

Run the case on the real tree and expect pass. Then `git worktree remove --force /tmp/own-mut`, which deletes only the throwaway worktree you created in this step. Run the shell suite ALONE; it is not concurrency-safe. Commit: `git add tests/test-scripts.sh && git commit -m 'test: owned sentinel blocks its own Stop (red-first)'`.

tasks.specExcerpt:
3. Add red-first cases to tests/test-scripts.sh for: owned, unowned (blocks), foreign (reports).

Goal context: an unowned sentinel must keep failing CLOSED.
North star: the Stop gate still blocks on mine + unowned. Missed if: … an unowned sentinel stops blocking.
steps: Create the fixture with the owned case's helpers. Make an unowned sentinel the way pre-0.4 did: run `bash scripts/ops-task.sh un1` with no --owner, and check whether that produces `pending/un1`. If ops-task.sh now refuses to run without --owner, create an empty regular file `pending/un1` with `: > pending/un1`; that is the legacy empty sentinel. Make sure the file name contains no `__`.
Pipe two payloads into ops-stop-hook.sh, one with session_id SID_A and one with SID_B. Reset `.operator/.stopguard/` between the two runs. `check` that BOTH exit with 2.

Red-first: in `git worktree add /tmp/unown-mut HEAD`, with the new test file copied in, edit `scripts/lib/partition.sh` so that `scan_pending` puts an empty owner (the unowned branch) into the foreign bucket. Run the suite there and expect this case to FAIL for both sessions. Then `git worktree remove --force /tmp/unown-mut`.
Run the suite alone on the real tree and expect pass. Commit: `git add tests/test-scripts.sh && git commit -m 'test: unowned sentinel blocks every session (red-first)'`.

tasks.specExcerpt:
3. Add red-first cases to tests/test-scripts.sh for: owned, unowned (blocks), foreign (reports).

CLAUDE.md: `ops-stop-hook.sh` blocks on _mine + unowned_ and merely reports _foreign_.
steps: Create the fixture: `bash scripts/ops-task.sh for1 --owner SID_B`, then pipe a payload with session_id SID_A into ops-stop-hook.sh and capture stdout+stderr. Find the foreign-report text with `grep -n 'foreign\|other session' scripts/ops-stop-hook.sh` and pin a stable substring of that echo. Also pin the task id `for1` in the output.
`check` that the exit code is 0 AND that the output contains the substring AND `for1`. Both assertions are required: exit 0 alone would also pass if the sentinel were simply never seen.

Red-first: in `git worktree add /tmp/for-mut HEAD`, with the new test file copied in, edit partition.sh `scan_pending` so a non-empty owner that differs from the session goes to the mine bucket. Expect exit 2, so the case FAILS. Then run a second mutation that drops the foreign report echo in ops-stop-hook.sh, and expect the substring check to FAIL. Afterwards `git worktree remove --force /tmp/for-mut`.
Run the suite alone and expect pass. Commit: `git add tests/test-scripts.sh && git commit -m 'test: foreign sentinel reports, never blocks (red-first)'`.

tasks.testCycle: `bash tests/test-scripts.sh 2>&1 | tail -3`: the new checks pass with 0 new failures. In a worktree where statusline.sh's BLOCKING count leaves out the unowned bucket, the case FAILS.
tasks.specExcerpt:
North star: Sentinel ownership lives where six readers and three writers agree on it, and the Stop gate still blocks on mine + unowned. Missed if: any reader and writer disagree on an owner.

CLAUDE.md: `ops-stop-hook.sh` (the gate) and `statusline.sh` (the bar) source [partition.sh] … a bar describing a different gate than the one that runs is worse than no bar.
steps: Read how the existing 'statusline segment reports the gate' case feeds `scripts/statusline.sh`: its stdin JSON and cwd, and the text of its blocking segment (`grep -n BLOCKING scripts/statusline.sh`). Reuse that invocation.

For each of three fixtures, run both ops-stop-hook.sh and statusline.sh as SID_A. The fixtures are: (a) `ops-task.sh m1 --owner SID_A`; (b) the unowned `pending/u1`; (c) `ops-task.sh f1 --owner SID_B`. `check` that the hook exits 2 exactly when the bar shows a non-zero blocking count: (a) and (b) block, (c) does not.

Red-first: in `git worktree add /tmp/bar-mut HEAD`, with the new test file copied in, remove the unowned bucket from statusline.sh's BLOCKING sum. Expect fixture (b) to FAIL. Then `git worktree remove --force /tmp/bar-mut`.
Run the suite alone and expect pass. Commit: `git add tests/test-scripts.sh && git commit -m 'test: bar and gate agree on sentinel owner (red-first)'`.

consumes: Case: sentinel owned by this session blocks its Stop
Case: unowned sentinel blocks every session (fails closed)
Case: foreign sentinel is reported, never blocks
Case: statusline and Stop gate agree on owner for mine, unowned, foreign
tasks.testCycle: `grep FLOOR_SHELL tests/floors.env` shows old value + delta. `bash scripts/gate-suite.sh <shell rung>` exits 0; get the rung name from `grep -n SUITE_RUNGS -A8 scripts/validate_plugin.py`.
tasks.specExcerpt:
5. Raise FLOOR_SHELL in tests/floors.env by the number of cases added.

CLAUDE.md: raise the matching `FLOOR_*` in `tests/floors.env` in the SAME commit… It is a FLOOR (`>=`) over **passed+skipped** (#109 — executor-invariant)… nothing raises it automatically.
steps: Measure the delta between the baseline from ownership-decision step 1 and `bash tests/test-scripts.sh 2>&1 | tail -3` now: (passed+skipped now) − (passed+skipped at baseline). The unit is whatever the floor counts, which is passed+skipped `check`s, not Case headers. Put the measured delta in the commit message.

Edit `tests/floors.env`: FLOOR_SHELL=<old + delta>. Then set it to the new total + 1 and run the shell rung through gate-suite.sh. Expect it to FAIL, which proves the floor bites. Restore the correct value.

Run the shell rung alone and expect exit 0. Commit: `git add tests/floors.env && git commit -m 'floors: FLOOR_SHELL +<delta> for sentinel ownership cases'`. The spec says to raise the floor in the same commit as the cases. If the reviewer requires that literally, squash this commit into the last case commit: `git rebase -i`, which is allowed on the feature branch.

tasks.title: Bump plugin.json to 0.13.0 with a matching CHANGELOG heading
files: CHANGELOG.md (insert `## [0.13.0]` as the newest heading, above the current top `## [x.y.z]`)
tasks.testCycle: `python3 scripts/validate_plugin.py; echo rc=$?` prints rc=0. The release gate passes (`ls scripts/release_gate*`, then run it). `grep -m1 '^## \[' CHANGELOG.md` prints `## [0.13.0]`.
tasks.specExcerpt:
4. Bump plugin.json to 0.13.0 and add the matching CHANGELOG heading.

CLAUDE.md: `plugin.json` `version` — add the matching `## [x.y.z]` as the newest heading in `CHANGELOG.md`, same commit (the release gate fails otherwise).
steps: Red first: change only `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` to "version": "0.13.0" and run the release gate. Expect FAIL because the CHANGELOG heading is missing.

Add `## [0.13.0]` at the top of CHANGELOG.md in the existing heading style (copy the date format from the previous entry). Write one entry: sentinel ownership stays in the filename, the body-field option is rejected (see the DECISIONS.md entry sentinel-ownership-filename), four red-first shell cases were added (owned, unowned, foreign, bar/gate agreement), and FLOOR_SHELL is raised by <delta>.

Run the release gate and the validator again, and expect both to pass. Then run every gate-suite rung, the shell rung ALONE. Run `shellcheck` on the changed shell files; CI runs it first and no rung covers it.

Commit both files together: `git add .claude-plugin/plugin.json CHANGELOG.md && git commit -m 'v0.13.0: sentinel ownership stays in the filename; owned/unowned/foreign cases'`. Push only with `git push -u origin feat/jev-decide`. Never push or merge to main.
